title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood inference performance vs the customer's current baseline provider. Covered latency (p50/p95), throughput/requests-per-second, tuning knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization), sequence length profiles, and next steps for focused benchmark runs and security docs. Action items assigned for follow-up benchmarks, security checklist, and scheduling a deep-dive with NovaHealth infra team.
topics: Benchmark results: latency and throughput vs baseline
Tuning strategies: batching, KV cache, quantization
Next steps: focused benchmarks, security docs, pilot timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we've got Priya, Marco, Sana from NovaHealth, and Liam and I from Redwood.
[00:22] Priya Singh: Hi, thanks. We ran the weekly benchmarks, excited to see where we landed.
[00:35] Liam Patel: Great, we'll walk through the numbers. I posted the benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmark/novahealth-week2 - see the 'summary' tab first.
[01:05] Marco Ruiz: Got it, opening now. Quick note, baseline runs are on CloudVendorX using their managed endpoint, default batching, KV cache disabled.
[01:30] Liam Patel: Important context, thanks. Ok first slide - p50 latency for the 2k token workload: Redwood (dedicated config) p50 approx 85ms, baseline p50 about 150ms. p95 Redwood 120ms vs baseline 220ms. These are median windowed numbers across 10k requests.
[02:05] Priya Singh: That p95 delta is promising. What GPU were you running on? Baseline is on A100-80GB, we think.
[02:25] Liam Patel: For Redwood tests we used a T4-equivalent node for parity in the pilot (we're testing quantized model variant too). Baseline claiming A100 but network overhead and no KV cache explain some of the gap.
[02:55] Sana Khan: Throughput numbers? Our key metric is steady-state rps.
[03:10] Ava Chen: Sure. Throughput: Redwood sustained 140-160 rps under continuous traffic with batching enabled and autoscaling rules; baseline peaked around 85-95 rps before latency increased.
[03:35] Marco Ruiz: Hmm that matches our observations, their burst handling is poor.
[04:00] Liam Patel: We also measured tokens/sec: Redwood ~12k tokens/sec effective on the workload shapes you provided; baseline ~7k tokens/sec.
[04:25] Priya Singh: Any quality tradeoffs for the quantized profiles?
[04:40] Liam Patel: We did int8 quantization with Redwood Optimize profiles; accuracy regression small — roughly 0.4% on the eval set you shared (intent classification F1 delta). We logged the full eval in the sheet.
[05:10] Priya Singh: Ok acceptable. Can you clarify what "batching enabled" meant in the test? We need reproducible steps.
[05:30] Liam Patel: Yes - we configured continuous batching with max batch size 64 and latency SLO 250ms. Also enabled dynamic batching which groups requests by model/route. We recorded average batching delay ~12ms.
[05:55] Marco Ruiz: Baseline probably used default small batch sizes; we didn't have explicit control in their managed UI.
[06:20] Ava Chen: Another lever was KV/prefix cache. We ran a subset with KV cache enabled and saw p95 latency improve by ~30% for repeat prefix requests. Baseline's managed endpoint doesn't expose KV cache.
[06:50] Sana Khan: That's interesting. For our use-case many requests share prefixes, so cache helps a lot.
[07:05] Liam Patel: Right - we show two curves in the sheet: 'cold' (no cache) vs 'warm' (cache hit rate ~65%). Warm runs had p95 80-90ms.
[07:35] Priya Singh: Were there any networking differences that could be skewing numbers? E.g., VPC peering vs internet.
[07:50] Liam Patel: Good call - for parity we ran Redwood in the same cloud region as your baseline tests but used our dedicated private routing; we also instrumented network RTT. Baseline had slightly higher RTT variance, about +10-20ms on average. We're adding a test with identical networking to isolate that.
[08:20] Marco Ruiz: Can you also show per-token cost comparisons? We care about unit economics.
[08:35] Ava Chen: Yes cost sheet included rough unit cost: Redwood optimized config shows ~30% lower per-token cost after factoring batching and Kv cache benefits vs baseline's managed endpoint, but final numbers depend on your reserved commit and traffic profile.
[09:00] Priya Singh: Good. Talk me through the tuning knobs you recommend we try next week.
[09:15] Liam Patel: Items: 1) Increase max batch size to 128 for high-concurrency tests (watch tail latency), 2) Enable KV cache with priming dataset, 3) Try mixed precision vs int8 to see the accuracy/latency sweet spot, 4) Run a network-controlled test where both endpoints sit in same VPC (to remove RTT variance).
[09:45] Sana Khan: For KV cache priming, how do we seed it? Do we upload prefix sets?
[09:55] Liam Patel: You can upload a list of heavy prefixes or run a warmup replay for 30-60 minutes. We'll share a script.
[10:15] Marco Ruiz: About the accuracy delta on quantization, can you share the eval harness? We saw 0.4% but need full confusion matrices.
[10:30] Ava Chen: Yes, full eval outputs are in the sheet and we'll push a linked artifact to the shared space.
[11:00] Priya Singh: Any stability issues during runs? Errors, OOMs?
[11:10] Liam Patel: No OOMs in Redwood runs; baseline reported occasional 503s under sustained burst. We logged error rates: Redwood <0.1% 5xx, baseline rose to 1.2% at peak.
[11:35] Marco Ruiz: That error rate is concerning for prod.
[11:45] Ava Chen: Agreed, that's why we focus on graceful degradation and fallback policies. We can demo automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if tails spike.
[12:05] Priya Singh: Security and compliance - did you collect logs for audit?
[12:20] Liam Patel: Yes, we enabled structured audit logs and showed KMS integration. We can export a sample audit trail for your SOC team.
[12:40] Sana Khan: We'll need SOC2 docs and SSO/SAML details before any production commit.
[12:55] Ava Chen: Understood - we'll share the security pack after the call.
[13:15] Priya Singh: On the baseline provider, are there differences in model variants used? Could explain throughput deltas.
[13:30] Liam Patel: We aligned on model family and tokenization but baseline ran a non-quantized state while Redwood tested quantized + mixed precision variants; yet even non-quantized Redwood runs beat baseline because of runtime kernel optimizations and batching.
[14:05] Marco Ruiz: Are the results reproducible across different sequence lengths? Our workloads vary 256-2k tokens.
[14:20] Liam Patel: We have per-length buckets in the sheet. For short seq (<=512) Redwood p95 ~70ms, baseline ~130ms. For long seq (~2k) both increase but Redwood maintains ~45% better throughput.
[14:50] Priya Singh: Good. What about cold-start latency if a model is scaled from zero?
[15:05] Liam Patel: Cold-start is dependent on instance spin-up; our Dedicated config keeps a small warm pool to avoid cold starts. Cold start to warm was ~9-12s in worst-case for a completely new pod; we recommend reserve instances for strict SLOs.
[15:35] Sana Khan: Ok noted. Anything else on infra?
[15:45] Ava Chen: We also flagged autoscaler tuning: a slightly more aggressive scale-up policy reduced 5xx at the cost of briefly higher infra burn during spikes.
[16:05] Priya Singh: Are there any limitations we should be aware of for VPC/private deploy?
[16:20] Liam Patel: For private on-prem we have a slightly different network stack — we'll schedule a security review call to go through SSO, KMS/HSM and audit log retention.
[16:45] Marco Ruiz: Can you run a test with the exact same model binary on both sides so we know runtime differences only?
[16:58] Liam Patel: Yes we can. We'll coordinate to mount the same model artifact. That'll isolate runtime/runtime ops.
[17:20] Priya Singh: Excellent. For next week, can you do two focused runs: 1) identical networking and model artifact parity, 2) KV cache primed test with warmup?
[17:35] Ava Chen: Yes. We'll run both and deliver a short report.
[17:50] Sana Khan: Timeline?
[18:00] Ava Chen: We'll execute tests by next Tuesday and share results by Wednesday EOD.
[18:20] Priya Singh: Sounds good. A couple quick clarifications: can you add cost anchors assuming our target of 5M tokens/day?
[18:35] Liam Patel: We'll add a cost projection in the sheet with batch and cache assumptions.
[19:00] Marco Ruiz: Also include per-route tracing so we can map latency to specific calls.
[19:15] Liam Patel: We'll enable tracing hooks and share sample traces.
[19:40] Priya Singh: Thanks. Anything else from Redwood?
[19:50] Ava Chen: We'll also propose a canary rollout plan for production cutover.
[20:05] Sana Khan: From NovaHealth, we'll confirm infra window for parity tests and share prefix list for cache priming.
[20:20] Priya Singh: Ok closing thoughts - this looks promising but we need the parity tests and security docs to move to a pilot contract.
[20:35] Ava Chen: Understood. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the deep-dive.
[20:45] *meeting ends*
next_steps: Redwood to run parity model artifact test and identical-network test by 2025-09-02
Redwood to run KV cache primed warmup test and share results by 2025-09-03
Redwood to share security pack (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration) by 2025-09-01
NovaHealth to provide prefix list for cache priming and confirm infra window by 2025-09-01
action_items: Ava Chen - Share benchmark report and cost projections - 2025-09-03
Liam Patel - Execute parity artifact and KV cache tests, upload traces - 2025-09-02
Priya Singh - Provide prefix list and confirm VPC window - 2025-09-01
Sana Khan - Review security pack and escalate any gaps - 2025-09-04
